observations: Black DSLR camera body with 'Nikon' and 'D7100' clearly visible on the front.
The camera is shown in front of a Nikon D7100 retail box in photo 0.
Photo 1 shows the camera body with the body cap removed, exposing the mirror and sensor area.
The seller's text claims the brand is Canon.
No batteries or silicone case are visible in the photos.

claims.evidence: Requires a video of the camera operating or sample photos.
Batteries are not visible in the photos.
The case is not visible in the photos.
Photo 0 shows Nikon branding on the camera body.

risks.proof: A screenshot of the shutter count from the last image's EXIF data.
A clear photo of the sensor and a sample image shot at f/22.
Photos of the back of the camera and a video of the menu being navigated.

proof_requests: Clarification on the brand discrepancy (Nikon vs Canon).
Photo of the back of the camera showing the LCD screen.
Photo of the 2 batteries and silicone case.
A recent photo file to check the shutter count.
response.reason: The seller's text identifies the camera as a Canon, while the photos clearly show a Nikon D7100. This fundamental error is a common sign of a scam using stolen images.
